programme.title: The Richard Dimbleby Lecture
programme.desc: Acclaimed actor David Harewood OBE delivers the 2023 Richard Dimbleby Lecture. On the 75th anniversary of the Empire Windrush arriving in Britain, David explores the challenges that were overcome by his parents' generation and considers their legacy.

programme.title: Being Beethoven
programme.desc: Beethoven embarks on a new creative path and attempts to find love. But, as is often the case, the composer's life appears to be following a very different trajectory to his art.

programme.title: Imagine...
programme.sub-title: This House Is Full of Music
programme.desc: A unique and intimate portrait of an exceptionally gifted musical family in lockdown: the Kanneh-Masons. In 2016, cellist Sheku Kanneh-Mason won BBC Young Musician award. In 2018, he released his debut album, and earlier this year his second album, Elgar, became a top ten hit. He achieved global fame when he performed solo at the wedding of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex in 2018 in front of a TV audience of two billion people worldwide.

programme.title: Secrets of Skin
programme.desc: Professor Ben Garrod explores the evolution of the body's largest organ, skin, starting with how the same basic structure has allowed vertebrates to conquer every corner of the planet.

programme.title: War Walks
programme.desc: Henry Tudor's dynasty toppled that of King Richard III, and Professor Holmes meets members of the Wars of the Roses federation who gather to re-enact the battle. He also talks to present-day supporters of Richard who are convinced he was not the soulless villain portrayed by Shakespeare.

programme.title: Burma, My Father and the Forgotten Army
programme.desc: Apart from a few fragmentary stories, Griff Rhys Jones' father never talked about his war. Yet as a medical officer to a West African division he travelled 15000 miles from Wales, to Ghana and the jungles of Burma. He and his men were part of an army of a million raised in Africa and Asia to fight the Japanese. To understand their story Griff travels first to Ghana and then to the jungles of Burma.

programme.title: The Nazis: A Warning From History
programme.desc: We reveal how a fear and hatred of Bolshevism drove many Germans to fight to the end, despite continued suffering. Germans from the former Eastern bloc describe the destruction unleashed by the collapse of the Nazi regime.

programme.title: Rise of the Nazis
programme.sub-title: Dictators at War: The Home Front
programme.desc: Facing defeat on the Eastern Front, Hitler retreats. Deep rifts emerge as his inner circle vies for power, the resistance gets a student voice, and an enemy within plots to kill Hitler.

programme.title: Storyville
programme.sub-title: Revenge: Our Dad the Nazi Killer
programme.desc: In a real-life murder mystery, three Australian brothers investigate whether their father and uncle, both Holocaust survivors, may have been involved in the deaths of former Nazis after the war.

programme.title: Colosseum
programme.desc: In 80 AD Emperor Titus opens the Colosseum with 100 days of spectacular games, including one of the most famous gladiatorial matches in Rome's history. After forming a close bond in their training school, two gladiators must now fight to the death.

programme.title: A Very British Romance with Lucy Worsley
programme.desc: Lucy Worsley concludes her series with the most dramatic transformation of romance yet. Out of the carnage of World War One came a racier species of romantic love. It could be found in the novel The Sheik, the Fifty Shades of Grey of its time, while in real life Marie Stopes urged husbands and wives to explore their sexual desire.

programme.title: The Real Jane Austen
programme.desc: Drama-documentary exploring the life of Jane Austen. Actor Anna Chancellor, a distant relative of Jane Austen, discovers the woman behind the acclaimed novels through readings and reconstructions. Location shots of her homes in Steventon and Chawton and extracts from adaptations of her work are also featured.

programme.title: Katherine Schlesinger Remembers... Northanger Abbey
programme.desc: Katharine Schlesinger looks back on the filming of the 1987 adaptation of Northanger Abbey, Jane Austen's ode to the gothic and her love letter to literature. Katharine talks about how this was her first on-screen role and considers the similarities between her personal experience and that of her character Catherine Morland, who is coming out into society for the first time.

programme.title: Northanger Abbey
programme.desc: A young girl, whose head is full of romantic and melodramatic notions, goes to stay with the wealthy Tilney family. Through her adventures, Catherine Morland comes to learn that marriage in the society of her day is determined not by true love but by wealth and social status.
